tweets.text:
context-bench is a benchmark for context-aware retrieval, created and privately held by @turbopuffer. Its queries, documents and capabilities are inspired by conversations with turbopuffer customers.

It has 2,099 queries and 38,894 documents. We submitted for blind evaluation. https://t.co/IsHUVOl4gh

We overcome gold-chunk supervision limits by distilling relevance from our query-aware context compression model.

It scores every document token against the query. Aggregated into chunk-level targets, those scores train the embedder to retrieve answer and supporting chunks. https://t.co/PvP2TLX5Y9

tweets.text:
The exact price is less meaningful than +-25% of frontier range. Of course, this is gameable by pricing high arbitrarily. And of course, you can’t avoid playing the benchmark game to avoid counter signaling.

But if you do price at frontier and do get meaningful usage uptick, I buy that it’s a good model!

Most if not all model companies pay benchmark companies to test their model and multiple versions of their model in advance of launch.

This is how benchmarking companies make money.

We’re at a point in late stage AI model capitalism where you know the frontier has to win in a bunch of benchmarks to launch. These numbers mean nothing.

The thing to trust is the price.

If they price it high, it’s a good model. If they don’t, it’s benchmaxxed.
